The elevated white blood cell count and anemia in the presence of a normal abdominal ultrasound suggest a hematologic malignancy rather than a solid tumor. I will request a peripheral blood smear to look for blast cells and a bone marrow biopsy to confirm the diagnosis.

The presence of smudge cells on the peripheral blood smear combined with lymphocytosis and anemia in an elderly patient is highly characteristic of Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia. I will confirm this with flow cytometry.

text:
The flow cytometry result is unexpectedly normal, which contradicts the classic presentation of CLL suggested by the smudge cells and lymphocytosis. I need to rule out other causes of lymphocytosis or potential lab errors, so I will request a repeat CBC with differential and a chest X-ray to check for mediastinal masses or other signs of lymphoma.
